body:
Closing after verification (2026-07-25): **the boundary this issue guards does not exist at runtime.**

- \`DataEngineRequestSchema\` ("Virtual ObjectQL", \`packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts\` §9) defines **request schemas only — there is no response schema at all**.
- **Zero runtime consumers** repo-wide (cloud included): no HTTP endpoint accepts these requests, and no remote proxy implements \`IDataEngine\`. The only implementation is the in-process ObjectQL engine (\`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts\`).
- The Virtual Data Engine therefore sits in the same "declared, no runtime consumer" family as GraphQL (#2605 / #3197). The update-side \`droppedFields\` gap is unreachable in every deployment topology that exists today.

**Design constraint to carry forward if/when a VDE is actually implemented** — treat this issue as an acceptance criterion for that work:

- The write-path RPC **response** contract MUST carry \`droppedFields\` (option 1 here), so the remote engine reports its own strips.
- Option 2 (recomputing update strips at the protocol layer via a pre/post diff) should **not** be built even then: it costs a pre-read per update and duplicates \`readonlyWhen\` predicate evaluation outside the engine — a permanent two-implementation drift tax.
- Option 3 (document the limitation) is already done: the schema comment on \`DroppedFieldsEventSchema\` states the listener cannot cross the RPC boundary.

Nothing to build until the VDE has a runtime.
